meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (unitary jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate or fiscal distinction)

DTAAs active with Luxembourg, Netherlands, Mexico, Singapore, Spain, and United Kingdom

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT framework), as amended; Law 129 of 2020 and Law 254 of 2021 (Final Beneficiary Register - Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, made fully public as of July 2023); Law 32 of 1927, as amended (Sociedades Anónimas); Ley 38 of 2000 (Administrative Procedure Act); Public Registry tariffs and DGI implementing resolutions for the UBO register.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport of each incorporator/subscriber and each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the subscriber's/UBO's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if origin is a 1961 Hague Convention member, as in force for Panama since 1991) OR Consular Legalization by a Panamanian Embassy/Consulate if origin is a non-member state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or corporate extract (where a subscriber is a legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the entity's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization via Panamanian consular authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of physical residential/business address for AML/KYC file (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certificate; apostille/consular legalization required when the KYC policy of the Panamanian resident agent so demands

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for each UBO and corporate subscriber
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank in the country of origin or a bank supervised by Panama's Superintendencia de Bancos
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-certified original; apostille is generally not required for AML file purposes

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified identity and capacity documents of pre-appointed directors and officers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, consulate, or competent authority of the director's/officer's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization by Panamanian consular authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all subscribers, UBOs, directors, officers and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU/UK sanctions lists, and the domestic designated list of Panama's Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF). PEP identification and enhanced due diligence per Law 23 of 2015, including 12-month post-employment EDD for former PEPs. Sanctions-list match triggers immediate client-relationship termination or freeze and statutory reporting to UAF; negative-news and adverse-media checks are part of standard onboarding approval.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Sede Electrónica (online name search and reservation system) — https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish is the official legal language; a corporate denomination may be drafted in Spanish or in any foreign language using Latin characters, but it must be distinctive, not identical, and not phonetically or graphically confusing with existing registered names. Foreign-language names must be accompanied by a transliteration or Spanish translation in the articles of incorporation and often require a Spanish-language alternative denomination. A suffix indicating limited liability (S.A., Inc., Corp., or the full phrase 'Sociedad Anónima') is mandatory.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco, Bank, Trust, Fiduciario, Fiduciary - requires prior authorization/license from the Superintendencia de Bancos
Seguros, Reaseguros, Insurance - requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros
Financiera, Finance, Fondo, Fondos de Inversión - requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia de Valores or the Superintendencia de Bancos
Nacional, Gobierno, República, Estado, Ministerio - implies official sponsorship and requires ministerial/executive authorization
Universidad, Colegio, Escuela, Academia - requires authorization from the Ministry of Education
Cruz Roja, Policía, Fuerza Pública, and other protected emblems/state symbols
Cooperativa - requires authorization from the Intendencia de Cooperativas
Names identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered entity, or contrary to law, morality, and public order
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The incorporating attorney obtains a name-availability certification ('Certificado de Búsqueda') through the Sede Electrónica or in person. If the name is rejected on grounds of confusion, similarity, or sensitive tokens, the attorney may file a 'Recurso de Reconsideración' before the Director General of the Registro Público within three (3) working days from notification under Ley 38 of 2000, and/or a hierarchical 'Recurso de Apelación' with the same deadline; alternatively, the attorney may submit a notarized non-opposition/consent letter from the holder of the conflicting name; after final rejection or expiration of the 30-day reservation, a fresh name search and new reservation may be filed without penalty.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissive for this unlicensed LegalTech SaaS industry: a virtual office may be used for general correspondence and administrative back-office, but it cannot replace the statutory registered office, which must be the physical Panama office of the licensed resident agent (agente residente) - a Panamanian lawyer or licensed trust company required under Law 32 of 1927. The resident agent must retain the physical registered address, governing documents, and share ledger at its Panama office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated under 5% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk standard S.A. The likelihood materially increases if the DGI economic-substance questionnaire, UBO register filings, or UAF AML inquiries reveal inconsistencies with declared activities or registered address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 32 de 1927 (General Law on Stock Corporations / Sociedades Anónimas), as amended; core formation provisions at Articles 5-7, capital structure rules at Articles 13-15, and registered-office/registered-agent duties at Articles 34 and 36.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección del Registro Mercantil (Sección Mercantil), Panama City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) containing the Pacto Social and corporate by-laws.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow deposit or pre-incorporation contribution is required. The standard S.A. is formed with authorized capital of US$10,000 divided into 10,000 registered shares of US$1.00 par value, payable as the Board determines; paid-in capital terms are set by the First Board Resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE COMPANY

WHEREAS, PA_CORP S.A. was incorporated under Panama's Law 32 of 1927 as a Sociedad Anónima; and WHEREAS, the undersigned directors form a lawful quorum.

IT IS UNANIMOUSLY RESOLVED:

1. Share Subscription. The authorized capital of US$10,000 (10,000 ordinary shares of US$1.00 par value) is hereby subscribed and issued to the founding shareholder as fully paid.

2. Registered Office. Fixed at [Calle 50, Torre BC, Oficina 2501, Panama City, Republic of Panama].

3. Officers. [Name], President and Legal Representative; [Name], Secretary; each vested with banking, commercial, and administrative authority.

4. The President is authorized to complete Public Registry registration, RUC registration, municipal licensing, and banking formalities.

Approved and signed this [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Departamento de Nombres (name-reservation counter and online portal).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit proposed corporate names for availability review; pay the official reservation tariff; receive a Name Reservation Certificate valid for 30 days. The same name must appear in the Escritura Pública to prevent duplication.
required_dossiers: Passport copy of incorporating shareholder or instructed counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is denied for identical/confusing similarity, promptly re-file using an alternative proposed name; a formal administrative request for reconsideration is available but re-filing is the commercially preferred cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarial Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura Pública)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Circuito, Republic of Panama (licensed Panamanian notary public).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the Spanish-language deed including corporate purpose, capital structure, board of directors, and by-laws. The incorporating shareholders or their attorney-in-fact appear personally before the notary, who verifies identity and legal capacity, reads the deed, and records it in the notarial protocol. Certified first-copy issuance follows immediately.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of incorporating shareholders and directors
Notarial power of attorney if executing through counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any detected defect is corrected through a notarial corrective instrument (adenda) or by re-execution before the same notary prior to registry filing; no re-notarization is required if the deed is not yet inscribed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Mercantile Section of the Public Registry (Folio Electrónico)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección Mercantil, Panama City.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Escritura Pública with the Mercantile Section together with the official tariff payment. The Registry conducts the legality review, assigns the company's Folio Electrónico, and issues the certificate of inscription. The company acquires legal personality upon registration; the issued Folio Electrónico serves as the master corporate certificate.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Escritura Pública
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defect notice (vista) is issued, the company's counsel submits written objections and corrective evidence within the statutory term; upon cure the inscription is completed, or the registry issues a final denial subject to judicial appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Registration — RUC and Corporate Tax File (DGI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) — Sede Electrónica online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the inscribed company with DGI to obtain the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) and corporate taxpayer file. Submit corporate existence data, legal-representative credentials, and domicile proof. The company is enrolled for income tax (ISR); ITBMS sales-tax registration applies only if taxable Panamanian services are rendered. An electronic tax-authority password is granted for filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rejection or suspension due to incomplete data is cured by correcting the online RUC application and resubmitting with the Folio Electrónico; if the portal remains unable to resolve, request an in-person DGI appointment at the corresponding Panama City office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating License and Ancillary Administrative Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá — Dirección General de Rentas (Ventanilla Única / 'Panama Tramita' portal); with MITRADEL and CSS for payroll.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Aviso de Operación / municipal business license at the municipality where the registered office is located. Attach the RUC certificate, Folio Electrónico, and lease evidence; obtain the Certificado de Uso de Suelo (zoning clearance). Register any employees with the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) and MITRADEL if payroll operations commence in Panama.
required_dossiers: Folio Electrónico of the Public Registry
Lease agreement or registered-office domicile title
Certificado de Uso de Suelo (zoning clearance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Query or denial is cured by settling any outstanding municipal fiscal obligations, correcting the business-activity classification to ISIC 6201, and resubmitting the complete dossier; formal reconsideration before the municipal tax directorate may be filed within the applicable appeal window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6201 (LegalTech SaaS and e-signature authentication) is a non-industrial digital service. Residual ICT supervision: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI), Dirección de Empresas; no industrial manufacturing board has jurisdiction.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial or operational manufacturing permit is required; the only operating permit is the municipal Aviso de Operación de Negocio (see SOP Step 5). E-signature authentication requires no additional sectoral license under Panama's digital-signature framework.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Normas y Evaluación Ambiental (DNEA).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I — Environmental Registration (Registro Ambiental) only; no full EIA/EsIA for office-based software activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater, VOCs, or point-source emissions are generated by cloud/SaaS operations. Any domestic-type discharges must meet the effluent limits of Executive Decree No. 508 of 2000; electronic and office wastes must be handled through MiAMBIENTE-authorized waste operators in accordance with Panama's general waste-management regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety inspection and certification by the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (Dirección de Prevención de Incendios); municipal structural and occupancy clearance through the Certificado de Uso de Suelo and building-safety inspection; occupational health-and-safety registration with MITRADEL and social-security enrollment of employees with the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas — national tax authority; digital portal: DGI Sede Electrónica (https://www.dgi.gob.pa; e-tax platform for RUC, ITBMS and corporate income tax filings).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Sociedad Anónima must obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) from the DGI. Steps: (1) appoint a Panamanian resident agent and legal representative in the notarial incorporation deed; (2) file the public deed, registration certificate from the Registro Público, and resident-agent acceptance through the Sede Electrónica; (3) submit Formulario 02-RUC and supporting bylaws (estatutos) plus fiscal domicile proof; (4) obtain the provisional RUC and, upon verification, the definitive RUC with an ITBMS (VAT) authorization; (5) register as an exporter of services in DGI's service-export registry if the SaaS/Automation services are rendered exclusively to non-residents; (6) activate electronic-invoice (Facturación Electrónica) certificate in the Sede Electrónica. No minimum capital requirement; non-resident ownership is fully permitted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope — the Panamanian S.A. is a taxable juridical person taxed on Panama-source income only (territorial principle). Foreign-source income is generally exempt, except where remitted to Panama, in which case the remittance basis of taxation applies. Not eligible for pass-through/check-the-box treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not implement a US check-the-box regime. Statutory options include: (i) election for the Régimen Opcional Simplificado (simplified presumptive income tax at 2% of gross revenues for taxpayers with annual gross receipts up to USD 200,000); (ii) election to apply the territorial remittance rule to foreign-source service income; (iii) election under Law 52/2023 to treat specified electronic/digital services (SaaS, e-signature, cloud automation) as sourced at the location of service use, with proof obligations on the provider; (iv) election to pay the optional 10% advance dividend tax; and (v) voluntary self-assessment in the DGI's Large Taxpayers (PGA) regime once turnover exceeds statutory thresholds.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) — a VAT-type consumption transfer tax on goods and services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de-minimis registration threshold — any person habitually transferring movable goods or providing services in Panama must register for ITBMS in the RUC and file monthly returns (Formulario FS-02) irrespective of turnover. The USD 200,000 threshold applies only to the optional simplified Income Tax regime, not to ITBMS registration. For a PA_CORP SaaS exporter without local clients, ITBMS registration is still mandatory for the zero-rated export declarations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory since September 2022 for all taxpayers: Facturación Electrónica (FE) must be issued through the DGI-authorized platform (Sede Electrónica DGI or certified third-party issuers). Every invoice requires real-time DGI validation, a unique electronic stamp (clave de comprobante digital) with QR code, and transmission to the DGI before fiscal use. Zero-rated exports must use the 'Exportación' invoice class with the digital export code; service-provider export declarations must be transmitted electronically. Automated billing via API-integrated TPAs is required for SaaS platforms; fiscal printing devices are no longer accepted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for services delivered to a non-resident and effectively consumed, used or enjoyed abroad, including LegalTech SaaS and e-signature authentication. Conditions: (i) the recipient has no permanent establishment or tax domicile in Panama; (ii) the service is executed/used outside Panama; (iii) the invoice is issued in USD (Panama's legal tender) without local ITBMS; (iv) payment is received from abroad and credited through the local banking system; (v) the reserved '0% Exportación' code is used in the electronic invoice. If services are used in Panama, the 7% (or 10% digital-services rate) applies to the Panama-source portion.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs/administrative export declaration for services (Declaración de Exportación de Servicios) when filed voluntarily or upon DGI request
Executed service contract with the non-resident purchaser clearly describing the offshore delivery model
Zero-rated electronic invoice with export digital stamp and QR code
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill or equivalent digital service delivery record (for goods; for SaaS, the server log and usage data evidencing offshore consumption)
Inward Remittance Certificate (certificado de remesa del exterior) issued by the receiving Panamanian bank evidencing FX inflows
Certificate of fiscal residence or foreign VAT/ID registration of the counterparty, where available
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may scrutinize export zero-rating claims for several years (statute of limitations generally 5 years, extended to 6+ years for non-declared refunds). The burden of proof lies on the exporter to demonstrate foreign use and actual repatriation. Upon audit challenge the DGI can: (i) claw back the zero-rating and assess full 7% ITBMS on the invoice amount; (ii) add a surcharge of up to 100% of the omitted tax (Código Fiscal Art. 762); (iii) impose per-invoice fines of USD 500 to USD 50,000 for incorrect electronic invoicing; (iv) initiate criminal proceedings for tax fraud (Art. 799-A) with imprisonment up to 10 years; and (v) suspend the taxpayer's RUC and CEDE (foreign-trade) authorizations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no traditional central bank, no domestic note issuance, and no central exchange-control authority. The United States Dollar is the de facto legal tender and monetary anchor, while the Panamanian Balboa exists solely as 1:1 subsidiary coinage. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panama (SBP) supervises all licensed banks and enforces AML/CFT rules under the General Banking Law (Decree Law 2 of 2008) and Law 23 of 2015. The Banco Nacional de Panama acts as the Republic's fiscal agent, clearing-house operator, and interbank settlement agent for the domestic ACH and the high-value payment system, giving the jurisdiction a fully dollarized, market-driven liquidity environment with no official FX intervention mechanism.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full free-market convertibility exists for both current-account and capital-account transactions in USD. The IMF regards Panama as a jurisdiction free of restrictions on payments and transfers for current international transactions. SaaS subscription revenue, shareholder capital injections, intercompany loans, royalty payments, and profit remittances may all move cross-border without quantitative FX limits or prior central-bank approval. Profit remittance is restricted only by tax withholding rules, not by FX controls: dividends from locally taxable profits generally face a 10% withholding tax, and a 5% rate applies to dividends from profits taxed under a preferential regime such as a Multinational Headquarters license. Dividends from purely foreign-source income can escape Panamanian dividend tax only when the territorial nature of the income is fully documented with contracts, issuer bank statements, and a coherent off-shore profit ledger; otherwise the DGI may impose a complementary levy. Practical hurdles are confined to OFAC sanctions screening, AML source-of-funds verification, and correspondent-bank validation of transaction purpose.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Panama imposes no surrender, mandatory conversion, or statutory repatriation timeline for export proceeds. USD receipts from SaaS services and electronic document-automation contracts may be retained freely in any SBP-licensed bank and redeployed for outbound disbursements without exchange-control approval. The operative compliance requirement is evidential, not monetary: the exporter must maintain the underlying foreign-client agreements, payment-acquirer settlement statements, and a clear reconciliation trail proving that the income is foreign-source under Panama's territorial tax system, thereby supporting the annual corporate income tax return (Form 150) and avoiding potential recharacterization of foreign income as local-source income.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational USD Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational USD Account and Treasury Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as an auxiliary rail, Low as a primary treasury layer. Panama does not issue EU-style Electronic Money Institution licenses and does not allow unlicensed foreign EMIs to obtain local IBANs or join the domestic ACH and SPAV clearing systems. Offshore digital banks and EMIs, including UK- or EU-authorized payment firms, may only operate on a sponsor-account basis through an SBP-licensed Panamanian bank or as non-bank money transmitters, which creates a 'conduit entity' profile that correspondents often flag. The recommended architecture is a Tier-1 Panamanian USD bank account as the settlement anchor for Stripe payouts and card-acquirer settlements, with EMIs confined to fringe functions such as vendor payables in non-USD currencies and back-office disbursement sub-ledgers. Over-reliance on EMIs as the exclusive bank relationship is not acceptable for a Panama S.A. seeking clean correspondent banking.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid and bank-specific. The standard SBP-aligned expectation for a foreign-owned Panama Sociedad Anonima is a face-to-face interview at the bank's Panama branch for the beneficial owners and for at least one statutory director. Several Tier-1 institutions will accept remote video onboarding where the company submits a notarized board resolution appointing a licensed Panamanian attorney-in-fact, provides apostilled corporate and shareholder documents, and allows the bank's compliance officer to conduct the interview via encrypted video conference. The mandate of physical appearance is not absolute: an in-person visit can be permanently waived if the director and beneficial owner pass a strict biometric call and the KYC dossier is pre-cleared, but for a first-time foreign S.A., most banks still require at least one physical signature and in-person presence within 60 days of account opening. Expect an onboarding cycle of 20 to 45 calendar days, depending on the origin of funds, beneficial-owner jurisdiction, and the quality of the documentary dossier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bearer-share or anonymous-ownership profile, including a Panama S.A. whose share register and beneficial-ownership filings are not updated with the Public Registry and the DGI Transparency Registry.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the registered shareholder ledger (Registro de Acciones) with physical share certificates held under safe custody; the sworn beneficial-ownership declaration (Declaracion Jurada de Beneficiario Final) filed with the DGI under Law 254 of 2021 and Executive Decree 129 of 2021; apostilled identification documents for every natural-person beneficial owner; a corporate structure chart showing no intermediate nominee secrecy; and a legal opinion from a Panamanian attorney confirming the chain of title.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undocumented operational existence, such as no RUC certificate, no municipal Aviso de Operacion, or no filed annual tax return despite active SaaS revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: DGI-issued RUC certificate; municipal Aviso de Operacion payment receipt for the operating district; certificate of tax good standing (Paz y Salvo fiscal); certified declaration of non-operation for the pre-revenue period; then, once active, the filed Form 150 return, audited financial statements, and evidence of local registered address and economic nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds anomaly, including a sudden shareholder capital injection from a third-country bank, a crypto-asset intermediary, or an unregulated payment wallet; also triggered when Stripe settlement volumes spike immediately after incorporation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements from the contributing shareholder; the notarized capital-subscription and board resolution authorizing the contribution; a source-of-wealth letter authenticated by an authorized public accountant (Contador Publico Autorizado); audited legal-entity financial statements or individual tax returns for the shareholder; precise Stripe settlement reports, card-acquirer invoices, and master SaaS agreements evidencing real commercial clients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or FATF enhanced-compliance nexus, including UBO or counterparty links to jurisdictions under the Financial Action Task Force grey list or to politically exposed persons in public procurement contexts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative sanctions and PEP screening results from OFAC, UN, EU, and UK HM Treasury lists; an independent AML risk assessment prepared by the on-boarding bank's compliance unit; a detailed transaction-flow chart for all inbound and outbound wire movements; enhanced due diligence documentation for every direct shareholder above the 5% threshold; and a written compliance attestation from an SBP-licensed compliance officer confirming that no red flags remain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The capital call is executed by the non-resident shareholder wiring USD from its home bank through global correspondent banks, typically JPMorgan Chase or Citibank New York, directly to the Panama S.A.'s USD operating or capital escrow account at the chosen Tier-1 Panamanian bank. The SWIFT MT103 message must carry the exact beneficiary corporate name matching the resolution, a complete originator account and address, and a clear field 70 narrative reading 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - APORTE DE CAPITAL - PA_CORP SOCIEDAD ANONIMA'. The transaction is cleared via Fedwire or CHIPS at the New York covering bank and credited to the Panamanian account as equity, not commercial income. The receiving bank will require the capital subscription sheets, the board approval minutes, and, for larger deposits above USD 100,000, a source-of-funds breakdown from the shareholder. Under Panamanian law, equity injections are not taxable, and the bank will code the credit as an equity inflow in its AML transaction-monitoring system rather than as an operating receipt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing relies on SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for all foreign vendor payments, SaaS subcontractor fees, and international disbursements; MT202 COV is used as the cover message for high-value same-day obligations. For settlements in USD inside Panama, the rails are the domestic ACH operated under the Banco Nacional de Panama and the high-value SPAV system, both clearing in USD with real-time final settlement. Stripe payouts and credit-card acquirer settlements arrive as daily or weekly USD sweeps into the operational account using the bank's standard settlement instructions, providing a predictable liquidity inflow. For clients or suppliers that require documentary trade instruments, Panamanian banks can issue and advise commercial letters of credit under MT700/MT710 and handle documentary collections under MT400/MT412, although this is atypical for LegalTech SaaS transactions, which normally settle on open account. Every outbound disbursement must be matched with a vendor invoice, attested service delivery, and sanctions-screened beneficiary identity to protect the bank's correspondent relationships.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forward contracts with a maturity of up to 12 months, booked with a Tier-1 Panamanian bank or its global parent, used to hedge EUR-denominated vendor invoices that exceed the SaaS company's EUR receivables.

USD/EUR FX swaps for short-dated liquidity bridging between the Panamanian USD operating account and a dedicated EUR disbursement float, protecting the treasury from temporary currency mismatches on intercompany recharges.

Cross-currency swaps on USD/EUR shareholder loans or acquisition notes, where the legal entity debt is denominated in EUR but the operative cash flows are USD; non-deliverable forwards are permissible only for ancillary exposure to regional Latin American currencies and must always be backed by a documented commercial or balance-sheet exposure, since Panama imposes no FX-control approval for derivatives but SBP and OFAC compliance remains mandatory.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate franchise tax 'Tasa Única Anual' (maintains S.A. legal existence and good standing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, through the Ventanilla Única electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March for each calendar year; no anniversary-based extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Payment after 31 March triggers a 10% surcharge plus accruing interest; repeated non-payment places the S.A. on the DGI public delinquent-taxpayer list, suspends issuance of 'Paz y Salvo' tax-clearance certificates, and blocks registration of corporate acts at the Registro Público. Law 32 of 1927 does not provide automatic administrative strike-off; chronic default leads to DGI judicial collection action and eventual court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholder and Beneficial Owner Declaration 'Declaración Anual de Accionistas' under Law 129 of 2020
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) via the mandatory Ventanilla Única e-filing module; resident agent submits on behalf of the S.A.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 March of each year, or within 30 days after the annual shareholders' meeting if held earlier; filing must present the shareholding and ultimate beneficial ownership structure as of 31 December of the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The DGI portal rejects the concurrent Tasa Única payment while the shareholder declaration is outstanding, freezing corporate good standing; Law 129 of 2020 provides fines from US$100 to US$5,000 on the company, directors, and the resident agent; three consecutive missed declarations result in suspension of corporate registration privileges and refusal to register share transfers at the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return 'Declaración de Renta IR-23' (including zero-activity 'sin movimiento' filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Sistema de Declaraciones Electrónicas (e-tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; calendar-year taxpayers must file on or before 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing triggers a formal-duty fine up to US$500, a 10% surcharge (recargo) on any tax payable, and monthly interest; the DGI may assess tax ex officio, publish the entity on the delinquent taxpayer list, and withhold 'Paz y Salvo' certificates required for share transfers, dividend distributions, and registrable corporate documents.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general statutory audit is imposed on private Sociedades Anónimas under Law 32 of 1927. A mandatory independent audit by a licensed Contador Público Autorizado applies only to: (i) issuers of publicly offered securities supervised by the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores; (ii) banks, trust companies, and licensed financial entities supervised by the Superintendencia de Bancos; (iii) insurance and reinsurance operators licensed by the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros; and (iv) taxpayers classified by the DGI as 'Grandes Contribuyentes' or otherwise required by DGI regulations to attach auditor-certified financial statements. The target LegalTech SaaS holding entity, being non-licensed and non-listed, does not meet the compulsory audit threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared and presented under IFRS as adopted by the Panamanian Comisión de Normas de Contabilidad; eligible small and medium entities may apply 'NIIF para PYMES' (IFRS for SMEs). DGI tax filings must be supported by IFRS-compliant accounting records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 129 of 2020, every S.A. must file an annual sworn electronic declaration of shareholders and final beneficial owners through the DGI Ventanilla Única. The declaration discloses all natural persons ultimately owning or controlling more than 10% of equity or voting rights, applying look-through treatment to nominees, trusts, and intermediate holding companies. The resident agent prepares and e-files the confirmation; submission is mandatory even in a year without share transfers, and any transfer executed during the calendar year must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the corresponding annual filing. Chronic failure to maintain the physical share ledger at the registered agent's office invalidates the UBO confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Officers (Registro de Directores y Oficiales)
Shareholders' and Board of Directors' Minute Books (Libros de Actas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$300–US$550 per annum (typical resident agent and registered office retainer charged by Panamanian licensed agent and trust firms)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$1,500–US$4,000 per annum for a full IFRS audit by a licensed Contador Público Autorizado; US$600–US$1,800 per annum for an accountant's compilation or review report where no statutory audit is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general holiday. Preferential 15% rate for multinational headquarters (SEM – Law 41 of 2007) and special zones (Panama Pacifico, City of Knowledge). Standard deductions for directly allocable Panamanian-source expenses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 121 (Personas Jurídicas) – Declaración de Renta; portal: DGI e-Dedaración at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 3 months after fiscal year-end (calendar year: March 31).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from Panamanian-source activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only revenue from services rendered or performed within Panama or to customers located in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs and deductible expenses attributable to Panamanian-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate expenses on a direct basis; global overhead must be prorated using a reasonable apportionment method.
Express the amount in USD/B/. in whole dollars.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at the 25% statutory rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No treaty reduction applies to the corporate headline tax rate.
Only Panamanian source withholding credits can be applied; foreign tax credits are not permitted under the territorial regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable after credits and payments (Box 4 − Box 5)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay through the DGI portal before the deadline; wire transfer must be in USD/B/.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance tax payments (Pagos Adelantados) to be declared
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must declare quarterly instalments based on the prior year’s tax or gross income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fine of 10% of tax due, plus monthly surcharge of up to 3% (maximum 100% of tax), plus legal interest. Persistent non-filing or under-filing can trigger administrative dissolution and tax registration suspension.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding on dividend distributions from Panamanian-source profits
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Present a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority to the Panamanian withholding agent. File DGI Form 730 (Solicitud de Doble Tributación) with the TRC and supporting ownership statements; treaty relief is granted upon DGI approval, after dividend distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 12.5% statutory. Interest: 12.5% statutory unless paid to recognized foreign banks or for trade finance (0%). Treaty rates may reduce royalties to 10% (e.g., Singapore) or interest to 5%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Local/Master File thresholds enacted. The Código Fiscal (Art. 702-A) mandates an arm’s-length standard for related-party transactions; documentation must be prepared and retained for audit, but there is no numeric threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not implement formal ESR for standard Sociedades Anónimas. However, entities must prove administrative and physical substance in Panama to claim tax residency or to avoid classification as a shell under Law 52 of 2016 (Beneficial Ownership Registry). OECD BEPS and FIU supervision impose practical substance requirements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or understatement of Panamanian-source revenue on Form 121, or false deduction claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine equal to 100% of the evaded tax plus interest; criminal penalties up to 5 years imprisonment under Código Fiscal Art. 702-B.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for tax, subject to civil restitution, travel bans, and asset seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Panamanian S.A. without any physical office, employees, or real business activity, used solely to divert intra-group invoices or hold assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalties up to USD 1,000,000 by the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) under Law 52 of 2016; corporate dissolution and tax disqualification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for restitution and face imprisonment up to 12 years under Panama’s anti-money-laundering regime.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify, register, and maintain current beneficial ownership information in the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Daily fine of USD 5,000 per day; criminal penalties of up to 5 years imprisonment for responsible officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally responsible for fines and may be barred from holding any Panamanian corporate office; travel bans apply pending enforcement.
